newsitem.title: LESOTHO: Lesotho braces for cereal shortage after drought.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho braces for cereal shortage after drought.

text.p: Lesotho is expected to suffer an estimated 300,000-tonne shortage of its staple maize and other cereals this year, the country's disaster management authority said on Friday.
The authority warned Lesotho inhabitants to stockpile grains ahead of severe winter conditions, after a dry spell in February stunted summer crop development and production.
Leteketa Molapo, the authority's chief executive, said preliminary estimates showed shortfall of some 216,000 tonnes of maize, 69,400 tonnes of wheat and 29,400 tonnes of sorghum.
"The cereal deficit will eventually have to be covered through commercial imports and/or by food aid from friendly countries," Molapo said.
The authority has warned that the self-sufficiency status of Lesotho is expected to deteriorate sharply this year.

The United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation representative in the country, Matthew Okai, blamed the smaller crop on the reduction in land suitable for agriculture and a depletion of soil fertility.
He said Lesotho lost about 40 million tonnes of topsoil each year due to soil erosion.
